newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares close up, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares close up, more gains seen.

text.p: Shares continued to rise on Lithuania's bourse on Thursday and brokers said the country's new credit rating would help boost its fledging markets.
Overall market volume was just over 1 million litas with the central market accounting for the lion's share with a turnover of 968,000 litas.
"This is a good sign. The central market was seldom more than 200,000 litas in the past but lately it has been responsible for most of the turnover," one broker said.
"The country's new credit rating should attract more interest to the central market," he added.
Lithuania was assigned a Ba2 rating for its foreign currency debt and a Ba3 for its bank deposits by Moody's Investors Service on Wednesday.
The young bourse has yet to introduce an official index but brokers said that their own informal indices showed a steady rise recently.
"Blue chip stocks have been rising," one broker said.
Vilniaus Bank, which is majority owned by Bankers Trust, saw its price rise 4.7 percent to 1,100 litas and 774,400 litas worth of its shares change hands.
Vilniaus Bank seems to have emerged unscathed from a crisis which shook the country's banking sector last year.
